title: Telemetry Tracking for the Average Home Racer (Race Management Display)
summary: Master telemetry tracking and race management displays for home sim racing. Improve lap times with real-time data analysis and professional-grade insights
body_text: In the rapidly evolving world of sim racing, telemetry systems now allow every sim racer to quickly acquire, analyze, and review detailed telemetry data from sim racing games, providing the same insights that real telemetry tools do for professional drivers. With the right race management display and telemetry tracking setup, average home racers can unlock performance improvements that were once exclusive to elite motorsports teams. Whether you're using a VelocityOne Race KD3 for entry-level direct-drive racing or the full VelocityOne Race system , Turtle Beach's racing ecosystem provides the foundation for serious telemetry analysis combined with immersive audio from the Atlas 200 Headset . What is a Race Management Display? A race management display represents the digital cockpit of modern sim racing, serving as your command center for real-time vehicle data and performance metrics. Advanced digital dashboards provide real-time race telemetry, full customization, and integration with popular racing titles to maximize immersion and improve performance. Modern race management displays integrate seamlessly with your existing racing setup. The Turtle Beach VelocityOne Race exemplifies this integration with its revolutionary Race Management Display™, which provides instant access to critical telemetry data without requiring you to look away from the track. Professional-grade telemetry software like vTelemetry PRO can acquire up to 104 data channels, including driver input data, chassis and suspension data, brakes and tires data, engine data, and 3-axes G-force measurements. This transforms your home racing setup into a miniature version of professional race team operations. How Telemetry Tracking Enhances Your Racing Performance Telemetry tracking fundamentally changes how you approach sim racing by providing objective, data-driven insights into your driving technique. By analyzing real-time data such as braking points, throttle input, and tire behavior, you can refine your technique and optimize your car setup, helping you achieve more consistent lap times. Professional-level telemetry tools capture data and illustrate exactly what happened on track, removing uncertainty from practice sessions. Instead of wondering whether you're losing time in braking zones or corner exits, the data provides concrete evidence of where improvements can be made. For home racers, telemetry tracking offers consistent development through pattern recognition, identification of specific areas for improvement, validation of setup changes, and the ability to compare your performance against faster drivers. The Turtle Beach VelocityOne Race KD3 exemplifies accessible direct-drive technology with integrated telemetry capabilities. VelocityOne™ Race KD3 Racing Wheel & Pedals View Product Essential Telemetry Metrics for Home Racers Understanding which telemetry metrics to prioritize can make the difference between overwhelming data overload and actionable performance insights. Key metrics include throttle and brake inputs, steering angle, tire temperature, suspension movement, and G-force measurements. Speed and Acceleration Metrics : Track speed variations across different sections to identify where you're gaining or losing time compared to optimal racing lines. Acceleration data reveals throttle application efficiency and helps optimize corner exit techniques. Brake Performance Data : Monitoring brake pad temperature and wear prevents failures while maximizing stopping power. Brake pressure and timing data help refine your braking zones and identify opportunities for later braking without compromising corner entry speed. Tire Management Telemetry : Tracking tire pressure and thermal fluctuations reduces degradation and improves grip balance. Temperature distribution across tire surfaces indicates whether your setup promotes even wear and optimal grip utilization. G-Force Analysis : Lateral and longitudinal G-force measurements provide insights into cornering efficiency and acceleration optimization. High-performance systems can analyze peak cornering G-forces and detect oversteer or understeer situations. The VelocityOne Race wheel system's Race Management Display™ provides immediate visual feedback of these critical metrics during racing sessions. Choosing the Right Telemetry System for Your Setup Selecting an appropriate telemetry system depends on your racing goals, technical comfort level, and budget considerations. Modern telemetry systems are available on PC, Mac, iOS and Android platforms. Entry-Level Solutions : For beginners, built-in telemetry features in racing games provide a solid starting point with basic telemetry overlays and data logging capabilities. Intermediate Systems : Professional-grade solutions like vTelemetry PRO offer up to 104 data channels and can record at high rates up to 330Hz for detailed analysis. Note that these capabilities require compatible software installations. Advanced Configurations : High-end systems integrate with professional analysis software and support real-time streaming to external devices. The Turtle Beach VelocityOne Multi-Shift demonstrates how simulation control systems can integrate with telemetry displays. Integrating Telemetry Data into Your Race Strategy Effective telemetry integration transforms raw data into actionable race strategy improvements. Real-time telemetry software allows racing teams to gather, analyze, and act on data instantly. Use historical telemetry data to establish baseline setups for different track conditions. Real-time telemetry enables dynamic adjustments to driving technique based on changing track conditions. Statistical analysis tools reveal patterns that might not be immediately apparent during racing. Racing wheels like the Turtle Beach VelocityOne F-RX Formula Wheel provide the precision control necessary to implement telemetry-based improvements effectively. Benefits of Real-Time Race Data Analysis Real-time data analysis represents the pinnacle of telemetry utilization for home racers. Modern systems successfully process and deliver millions of messages in under a second. For the Rolex 24, 6.5 million messages were successfully processed and delivered. Real-time systems provide instant validation of technique changes, allowing you to see the impact of driving adjustments immediately. Real-time telemetry empowers drivers to fine-tune systems by monitoring critical parameters and preventing failures. Professional-grade real-time analysis tools level the playing field between amateur and professional racers. Common Challenges with Home Racing Telemetry Systems Despite their benefits, telemetry systems present challenges that home racers must navigate successfully. Telemetry can be difficult to read for novice drivers, making user-friendly platforms essential for effective analysis. Focus initially on three to five key metrics rather than attempting to analyze every available parameter simultaneously. Telemetry display compatibility varies significantly between games and platforms. Xbox versions of some games may have limited telemetry display support compared to their PC counterparts. Always verify telemetry compatibility with your preferred racing titles before investing in advanced display systems. Many telemetry systems require significant configuration. Budget time for initial setup and expect a learning curve as you become familiar with the software interface and data interpretation. The Turtle Beach VelocityOne Multi-Shift exemplifies well-designed hardware that integrates smoothly with telemetry systems while providing additional control options. Tips for Maximizing the Use of Your Race Management Display Optimizing your race management display requires strategic configuration and disciplined analysis habits. Having real-time data on screen helps you make quick adjustments mid-race. Prioritize the most actionable telemetry data on your primary display. Essential metrics typically include current lap delta, tire temperatures, fuel remaining, and position information. Start with basic telemetry parameters and gradually incorporate more complex data as your interpretation skills develop. Establish regular review sessions to analyze telemetry data and identify improvement opportunities. The VelocityOne Race bundle offers integrated precision control that ensures your inputs are accurately reflected in telemetry data, providing reliable feedback for performance analysis. Conclusion Telemetry tracking and race management displays have democratized access to professional-grade racing analysis tools, enabling average home racers to achieve performance improvements that were once exclusive to elite motorsports teams. With patience and the right approach, telemetry becomes your personal coach. Products like the Turtle Beach VelocityOne Race demonstrate how integrated telemetry systems can enhance the home racing experience while providing the data insights necessary for continuous improvement. As sim racing technology continues to evolve, telemetry tracking will remain a critical tool for competitive advancement. For more insights, explore our guide on magnetic paddle shifters for Xbox and PC racing , or learn more about direct drive racing wheel technology to complement your telemetry setup. Frequently Asked Questions What does a race management display do? A race management display serves as your digital cockpit, providing real-time access to critical vehicle performance data, including speed, RPM, tire temperatures, fuel levels, and lap timing information. Modern displays integrate seamlessly with racing simulation software to deliver professional-grade telemetry capabilities. How can telemetry improve my racing lap times? Telemetry provides honest feedback by illustrating exactly what happened on track during each lap. By analyzing braking points, throttle application, and cornering speeds, you can identify specific areas where time is being lost and develop targeted improvement strategies. What telemetry data is most important for casual racers? Focus on fundamental metrics including lap times and sector splits, brake and throttle inputs, tire temperatures, and basic vehicle speed data. These core parameters provide actionable insights without overwhelming newer users. How do I install telemetry tracking for my racing simulator? Most modern telemetry systems offer straightforward installation processes that involve downloading compatible software and configuring it to work with your preferred racing games. Systems support data acquisition from PC, PlayStation, Xbox, and Mac platforms. Note that advanced telemetry features may require developer support and game-specific integration for full functionality.

title: How to find out if your insurance covers genetic testing
body_text: Does Insurance Cover Genetic Testing? What They Refuse to Tell You (And What We're Doing About It) ‍ Highlights Insurance coverage for genetic testing depends on 10+ factors, including your insurance provider, plan, symptoms, diagnoses, ordering physician, and medical justification. Insurance companies rarely explain these factors clearly. Many private insurance plans cover whole exome sequencing when medical necessity criteria are met , but families often receive vague denials without clear explanations of what would qualify. Our free 30-second assessment tells you if coverage is likely based on your insurance, symptoms, and ordering physician, and then connects you with free genetic counseling if eligible. Symptom combinations matter more than you'd think : Insurance approves "seizures + developmental delays + low muscle tone" at higher rates than "developmental delays alone," even when investigating the same genetic cause. Who orders your test significantly impacts approval : Referrals from genetic counselors or geneticists receive higher approval rates than orders from general practitioners. The average diagnostic odyssey takes 5-7 years1 . That's years lost navigating insurance bureaucracy instead of getting answers. ‍ I'm tired of watching families struggle to get straight answers about genetic testing coverage. ‍ After years of working with thousands of patients navigating the healthcare maze, I've seen the same story play out over and over. Someone suspects their child has a genetic condition. Their symptoms don't fit neatly into a predefined box in clinical care guidelines. And when they ask their insurance company whether genetic testing is covered, they get... nothing. Vague policy language. Endless hold music. Denials that don't explain what would have been approved. ‍ The system is designed to be confusing. And it's costing families years of answers. ‍ The average diagnostic journey for a rare genetic condition takes 5-7 years. That's 5-7 years of watching your child struggle while doctors run test after test, never quite finding the answer. Meanwhile, the one test that could actually provide clarity, comprehensive genetic sequencing, otherwise known as whole-genome or whole-exome sequencing, sits just out of reach, buried under insurance bureaucracy no one will explain. ‍ Patients and their families deserve better than this labyrinth. So we built something to help. ‍ Why is Insurance Coverage for Genetic Testing Impossible to Understand? Here's what insurance companies don't tell you upfront: whether your genetic test gets covered depends on ten or more different factors , and most of them aren't written down anywhere you can easily find. Your coverage depends on: Which insurance company you have (Aetna handles things differently than Blue Cross, which is different from Cigna, which is different than government-insured programs like Medicare) Which plan you have with that insurance company What your symptoms are (seizures get treated differently than developmental delays) Whether you have a diagnosis already (having an autism diagnosis changes everything compared to "unexplained developmental delays") What testing has been performed previously (insurance companies look for proof that simpler testing has been performed to rule out options prior to considering coverage for comprehensive sequencing Who orders the test (a geneticist's order carries more weight than your pediatrician's) Why they're ordering it (diagnostic testing vs. carrier screening vs. family planning all have different rules) What type of test they're ordering (whole exome sequencing vs. single-gene panel vs. chromosomal microarray) And that's just the beginning. ‍ The Real Numbers Behind Insurance Coverage Denials The statistics tell the story insurance companies would rather you not see: ‍ Many major insurance plans do cover genetic testing when it's deemed medically necessary, but getting to that determination is where families hit walls. Recent analyses of U.S. commercial plans suggest that roughly 50% (half) of insured individuals have coverage for exome sequencing (with or without genome sequencing) when medical-necessity criteria are met2, while others may not have adequate coverage. How do you know what those criteria are? Finding them spelled out clearly is no small task. ‍ Medicare also covers genetic testing for specific conditions when ordered by a qualified healthcare provider and deemed medically necessary, but what qualifies as "medically necessary" changes based on your situation, your symptoms, and frankly, how well your doctor knows how to navigate the system. ‍ Here's what happens all too often: families spend months gathering documentation, getting referrals, waiting for appointments with specialists, only to submit for pre-authorization and receive a denial letter stating that their case "doesn't meet medical necessity criteria," without explaining what would. ‍ What Actually Matters for Insurance Coverage (That No One Tells You) Partnering with the best clinical, CAP/CLIA-accredited reference labs in the country, as well as telehealth providers and physicians that specialize in genetic testing for rare conditions, we’ve learned a thing or two about what moves the needle. ‍ Your symptoms matter more than you think. Insurance companies consider specific symptom combinations that suggest a genetic cause. If your child has seizures plus developmental delays, plus low muscle tone, that pattern carries weight. But "just" developmental delays? Much harder to get approved, even though the underlying cause could be exactly the same. ‍ Previous diagnoses can help or hurt. If your child already has an autism diagnosis, that can actually make it easier to get genetic testing covered, but only if the right medical justification is used. A diagnosis of "global developmental delay" without specifics? That can be treated as not specific enough. ‍ Who orders your test matters enormously. A referral from a genetic counselor or a medical geneticist carries more weight than orders from a general practitioner, even when they're seeking the same answers. ‍ The medical reason matters. Testing for a specific suspected condition is approved at higher rates than testing for "rule out genetic causes," even if the clinical picture is identical. ‍ We Built a Tool Because We Were Tired of Waiting for the System to Change I wish I could tell you that insurance companies will suddenly become transparent about their coverage policies. I wish I could say that next year, it'll be easier to get straight answers. ‍ But I can't. Collectively, our team and the experts we partner with have been at this for a long time, and our health system is slow to change. ‍ So we built something different: a 30-second assessment that tells you whether insurance coverage might be possible for your situation. ‍ It's free. It's fast. And it asks the questions that actually matter: What insurance do you have? (Because Aetna's policies are different from Medicare's, which are different from Blue Cross's) What symptoms or diagnoses are present? (Because "seizures" gets coded differently than "epilepsy," which gets coded differently than "seizures with developmental delays. ") Who might order the test and why? (Because these factors change everything about approval likelihood) Take the 30-second insurance coverage assessment → ‍ What Happens After You Complete the Assessment Here's what makes this different from calling your insurance company: ‍ If coverage looks unlikely for your current situation , we'll let you know and give a brief explanation of why. Maybe you need a more specific diagnosis first. Maybe you need a referral to a geneticist who can provide better documentation. ‍ If coverage looks possible or likely , we'll let you know. And, if you want, we can connect you with a board-certified genetic counselor for a free telehealth appointment to actually pursue that coverage. Just create a profile with Probably Genetic and add the same information that you share with the assessment tool. ‍ Our telehealth and lab genetics experts will: Review your specific insurance policy Help gather the documentation you need Submit the necessary paperwork to support pre-authorization Order testing with the clinical laboratory if you decide to move forward Appeal on your behalf if insurance denies ‍ This Shouldn't Be This Hard (But Until It Changes, We're Here to Help) Here's what I know after years in this space: people shouldn't need to become insurance policy experts just to get answers about their health. ‍ You shouldn't need a medical degree to understand whether genetic testing is covered. You shouldn't need to make dozens of phone calls to different departments, repeating your or your child's symptoms over and over, just to find out if insurance will help. ‍ The system is broken. We can't fix the whole system overnight. But we will keep building tools and services to help you navigate the system more easily, faster, and with better results. ‍ Take the Next Step Take 30 seconds to complete our insurance coverage assessment. Answer a few questions about your insurance, your symptoms or diagnosis, and your situation. Finally, answer that burning question, “How to know if genetic testing is covered by insurance?” and if it is, get connected with a genetic counselor who can actually help you pursue it. ‍ Complete the insurance coverage assessment → ‍ Still not sure if genetic testing is right for your situation? Our genetic counselors can help you understand that, too. The telehealth consultation is free, whether or not your insurance covers the test. ‍ The Questions You're Probably Asking Does this assessment guarantee coverage? No. Only your insurance company can approve coverage. But this assessment is built on patterns from patient cases, and it can tell you whether coverage is likely, possible, or unlikely based on your specific situation. ‍ What if my insurance isn't listed? Most major commercial and government-insured options are included, such as Aetna, Blue Cross Blue Shield, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, Medicare, Medicaid, and smaller plans. If yours isn't listed specifically, it will be harder for us to offer coverage insights at this time. However, if you create a profile with Probably Genetic, you may still have the opportunity to speak with a genetic counselor. ‍ Is the genetic counseling appointment really free? Yes. Whether insurance covers your test or not, the genetic counseling consultation is free for eligible patients with a Probably Genetic profile. We believe families deserve expert guidance to navigate these decisions. ‍ What if insurance doesn't cover the test? You can discuss alternative options with the genetic counselor and/or the laboratory, including the Probably Genetic free genetic testing programs for specific conditions, research opportunities, and self-pay options if that is of interest. ‍ How long does this process take? The assessment takes 30 seconds. If you qualify for a genetic counseling appointment, those are typically scheduled within a week. Insurance pre-authorization timelines vary, but our genetic counselors know how to navigate the process efficiently. ‍ Wishing you and your family find the answers you are looking for, Caty ‍ The diagnostic journey is hard enough without insurance bureaucracy making it harder. Let us help you determine whether coverage is possible and connect you with experts who can make it happen. Get started with the insurance coverage assessment → ‍

title: Social commerce and mobile shopping: how Gen Z is reshaping global e-commerce
summary: In 2025, Gen Z emerged as the most influential consumer segment in global e-commerce—and nowhere was this more evident than in Latin America.
body_text: Mariana González Senior Marketing Analyst – PagSeguro December 30, 2025 In 2025, Gen Z emerged as the most influential consumer segment in global e-commerce—and nowhere was this more evident than in Latin America. With over 150 million Gen Z consumers across the region, their mobile-first, social-first habits are redefining how brands engage, convert, and retain customers. This generation doesn’t just shop online—they live online. Their expectations for speed, authenticity, and seamless experiences are setting new standards for global merchants. Latin America’s digital landscape is uniquely suited to Gen Z’s preferences. The region boasts over 80% smartphone penetration and some of the highest social media engagement rates in the world. Platforms like TikTok, Instagram, and WhatsApp are not just communication tools—they’re discovery engines, shopping channels, and trust-building platforms. For merchants, adapting to Gen Z means rethinking everything from UX design to payment flows to influencer strategy. To succeed in this evolving landscape, global brands must meet Gen Z where they are: on mobile, on social, and with payment experiences that feel native. Here’s how Gen Z is reshaping e-commerce—and how PagSeguro is helping merchants keep up. Mobile-first habits and social discovery Gen Z’s shopping journey starts—and often ends—on their smartphones. In Latin America, over 70% of e-commerce traffic now comes from mobile devices, and Gen Z leads this trend. They expect fast, intuitive mobile experiences that mirror the ease of social media interactions. Slow load times, clunky checkouts, or non-optimized pages are instant deal-breakers. Discovery is deeply social. TikTok, Instagram, and WhatsApp are the new storefronts, where Gen Z browses, shares, and buys. TikTok alone saw a 45% increase in LATAM-based product discovery in 2025, with short-form videos driving impulse purchases and brand awareness. Instagram’s shopping features and WhatsApp’s business integrations have made it easier than ever for users to move from conversation to conversion. For merchants, this means designing mobile-first experiences that integrate seamlessly with social platforms. It’s not enough to be present—brands must be optimized for the way Gen Z shops: fast, visual, and frictionless. Trust through creators Gen Z doesn’t trust traditional advertising. Instead, they look to creators—micro and macro influencers who reflect their values and lifestyles. In Latin America, 60% of Gen Z consumers say they’re more likely to buy from a brand recommended by an influencer than one they see in a paid ad. Authenticity is key: scripted content and polished campaigns often fall flat. Local influencers play a critical role in building credibility. Whether it’s a fashion creator in São Paulo or a tech reviewer in Mexico City, these voices help brands connect with Gen Z on a personal level. Merchants who invest in long-term influencer partnerships see stronger engagement, higher conversion rates, and deeper brand loyalty. PagSeguro supports merchants in identifying and activating local influencer networks, helping brands build trust through content that feels native, relevant, and real. In a market where authenticity drives action, creators are the new currency. How to leverage the new online consumer behavior To meet Gen Z’s expectations, merchants must rethink their digital infrastructure. PagSeguro offers mobile-optimized checkout experiences designed for speed and simplicity. These checkouts are built to reduce friction, with intuitive design and fast load times that align with Gen Z’s mobile habits. Local payment methods are essential. Pix in Brazil, SPEI in Mexico, and PSE in Colombia are not just popular—they’re expected. In 2025, Pix accounted for over 70% of ecommerce payments in Brazil, and merchants who offered it saw conversion rates up to 60% higher than those who didn’t. PagSeguro integrates these methods natively, ensuring seamless transactions that feel familiar to Gen Z shoppers. Social commerce compatibility is another key differentiator. PagSeguro enables merchants to embed payment flows directly into platforms like Instagram and WhatsApp, allowing users to complete purchases without leaving the app. This frictionless experience is critical for Gen Z, who value speed and convenience above all. Winning Gen Z in Latin America: A Strategic Checklist To succeed with Gen Z in Latin America, global merchants should: Streamline mobile UX with fast, intuitive design that mirrors social media behavior. Offer local payment options like Pix, SPEI, and PSE to boost conversion and trust. Build influencer partnerships with creators who resonate with Gen Z values and lifestyles. Gen Z is shaping the future of ecommerce. They’re mobile-native, socially driven, and authenticity-obsessed. Merchants who adapt to these behaviors will not only capture attention—they’ll earn loyalty. With PagSeguro, global brands can localize their strategy, simplify payments, and connect with Gen Z in ways that drive real results. title: AAON Activates Accordion Feature on Credit Facility to Support Growth
summary: AAON activates accordion feature on credit facility, increasing borrowing capacity to $600 million to support growth and meet customer demand.
body_text: TULSA, OK, December 29, 2025 – AAON, Inc. (NASDAQ: AAON) (“AAON” or the “Company”), a leader in high-performing, energy-efficient HVAC solutions that bring long-term value to customers and owners, today announced that it has exercised the accordion feature on its existing revolving credit facility, increasing the Company’s available borrowing capacity to $600 million. This strategic move provides additional financial flexibility to meet accelerating customer demand and support ongoing growth initiatives. “Our business continues to experience strong momentum with bookings strength continuing throughout the fourth quarter, driven by robust market conditions and expanding customer needs,” said Rebecca Thompson, CFO and Treasurer. “Activating the accordion feature ensures we have ample liquidity to invest in growth and respond to demand, while maintaining a disciplined capital structure.” The accordion feature, negotiated as part of the Company's credit agreement, allows the Company to expand its borrowing limit without renegotiating the entire facility. This increase strengthens the Company's ability to fund working capital, capital expenditures and strategic projects aligned with its long-term growth objectives. AAON Founded in 1988, AAON is a world leader in HVAC solutions for commercial and industrial indoor environments. The Company's industry-leading approach to designing and manufacturing highly configurable equipment to meet exact needs creates a premier ownership experience with greater efficiency, performance and long-term value. AAON is headquartered in Tulsa, Oklahoma, where its world-class innovation center and testing lab allows AAON engineers to continuously push boundaries and advance the industry. For more information, please visit www.AAON.com. body_text: Starting your streaming journey feels overwhelming when you're staring at endless gear lists. You want quality content, but figuring out where your money should go first? That's the real challenge. Here's the thing, though: building a killer streaming setup doesn't mean emptying your wallet on day one. The live streaming equipment market tells the whole story. Growing from $11.04 billion in 2024 to $12.08 billion in 2025, with projections hitting $19.03 billion by 2030 , this isn't just a trend anymore. Content creators everywhere are stepping up their game, and the right foundation puts you right there with them. Audio Quality Isn't Negotiable Here's what separates successful streamers from the rest: they get audio right from day one. Viewers will tolerate wobbly video quality, sure, but bad audio? They're gone before you finish your intro. Those built-in webcam mics and basic gaming headset microphones work fine for Discord chats, but streaming demands something better. The Stealth 700 Gen 3 changes everything for content creators. This isn't just another gaming headset with streaming pretensions. The CrossPlay wireless system delivers dual USB transmitters that let you switch between platforms instantly, while simultaneous Bluetooth means Discord monitoring without audio gymnastics. That 80-hour battery life? Marathon streaming sessions become reality, not wishful thinking. The AI-powered noise reduction microphone here rivals dedicated streaming mics costing twice as much. It's genuinely impressive how clean your voice sounds even in less-than-perfect environments. Budget tighter than you'd like? The Stealth 600 strips away some premium features but keeps the essential audio quality that makes viewers stick around. No shame in starting here and upgrading later. For mobile or travel content, the Atlas Air delivers lightweight comfort with an open-back design that's perfect for music-focused streams. Sometimes less weight means more streaming hours. Visual Setup That Actually Works Your camera creates the connection viewers want, but here's the catch: smartphone cameras work better than most people think for starting out. Research shows 85% of content creators prioritize visual upgrades , but rushing into expensive cameras before nailing your content style? That's backwards thinking. Lighting transforms everything. Seriously, everything. Position lights at 45-degree angles, eliminate harsh shadows, and watch average-looking content become professional overnight. A green screen removes background chaos and keeps focus where it belongs: on your content. The real game-changer? Understanding that visual polish comes from consistent setup, not the most expensive gear. Controllers That Elevate Your Content Gaming content demands precision that translates to viewers. The Stealth Ultra Controller delivers tournament-level performance with wireless freedom. When every input matters for competitive content, this controller eliminates the "my equipment failed me" excuse. Fighting game content? The Victrix Pro KO leverless fight stick represents cutting-edge performance that serious fighting game viewers notice immediately. Understanding leverless vs traditional differences helps match your equipment to your content vision. The Stealth Pivot Controller excels at versatility. Mobile games, PC titles, and different genres throughout single streams? This controller adapts seamlessly without forcing awkward transitions. Specialized Content Demands Specialized Gear Racing simulation content without proper equipment looks amateur instantly. The Velocity One Race wheel creates authentic experiences that racing enthusiasts recognize immediately. Magnetic paddle shifters add precision that translates directly into engaging content. Flight simulation requires dedicated equipment like the Velocity One Flight system . Aviation content without proper controls feels forced and unconvincing. Music streams get instant credibility with the Riffmaster wireless guitar controller . Rhythm game performances become entertainment rather than just gameplay footage. Your Foundation Determines Everything Before buying anything else, test your internet connection thoroughly. More than 850 million households globally adopted streaming devices , but all that equipment becomes an expensive decoration without stable connectivity. Skip Wi-Fi entirely if possible. Ethernet connections eliminate wireless interference and provide consistent speeds that streaming demands. Test upload bandwidth specifically since streaming pushes data constantly. Target 10 Mbps minimum for 1080p at 60fps, but higher is always better. Essential Peripherals That Actually Matter The Vulcan II Max keyboard provides tactile feedback and durability that survives intense gaming sessions. Wireless connectivity keeps desk organization clean without sacrificing performance. Creating an ultimate couch gaming setup opens content possibilities beyond traditional desk configurations. An extended wireless range means flexibility that translates into more engaging content options. Budget-Smart Approaches Thousands upfront isn't realistic for most streamers, and honestly? It's not necessary. The Stealth 500 provides excellent entry-level audio without premium pricing. Start here, build your audience, then reinvest earnings into upgrades. Audio improvements deliver the biggest impact for new streamers. Viewers tolerate video issues but abandon streams with poor audio faster than anything else. Upgrade audio first, always. When choosing between wireless and wired options , consider your content style and streaming environment. Wireless offers movement freedom, while wired provides zero-latency audio crucial for competitive content. Conclusion The streaming equipment market expansion reflects content creation becoming mainstream rather than niche. Smart equipment choices and strategic upgrades build professional setups that grow with your channel while respecting budget realities. FAQs What's the most important streaming equipment? Internet connection, full stop. Premium equipment means nothing without stable connectivity. After that, audio quality determines whether viewers stay or leave. Can I start streaming without expensive gear? Absolutely. The Stealth 600 provides excellent starting audio quality. Build your channel first, then upgrade strategically based on what your content actually needs. How do I choose the right controller? Match equipment to content focus. Stealth Ultra works for general gaming, Victrix Pro KO suits fighting games specifically. Equipment should enhance your content, not define it. What's the smartest upgrade path? Audio first, always. Then lighting and visual improvements. Specialized controllers and peripherals come after you understand your content style and audience preferences.

title: Overseas Clothing Production: Finding the Right Factory Fit
summary: Learn how boutique brands choose countries and factories for overseas clothing production, plus what drives delays, rework, and version confusion.
body_text: Overseas clothing production typically means that some or all of your boutique brand's or micro-studio's development and manufacturing occur outside your home country. It can bring real upside: specialized factories, more capacity, and often better unit economics. The tradeoff is coordination. Time zones, unclear approvals, and “almost clear” specs can turn simple decisions into extra sampling rounds and timeline drift. Overseas clothing production tends to run more smoothly for small teams when it’s treated less as a one-time handoff and more as shared clarity. Before we jump in: With AI Techpacks, you can generate tech packs automatically using a photo and a few key details as a starting point. It’s also built to save time by centralizing product specs and making them easier to share, reducing avoidable back-and-forth and version confusion once sampling starts. In Practice, Much Depends on How Responsibilities Are Distributed You’ll often hear the following. CMT (cut, make, trim): you supply more of the key inputs (often patterns; sometimes materials), and the factory assembles. FOB (Free on Board): an Incoterm that’s sometimes used in apparel to describe more bundled quotes. What’s included varies, so it’s worth clarifying whether materials, trims, packaging, freight, and duties are part of the quote. Full package: the factory (or partner) supports more end-to-end steps, sometimes including development support and sourcing. These labels aren’t universal. They’re best treated as starting points, with the specifics confirmed in writing. Most overseas production still follows the same broad arc: specs, sampling, pre-production alignment, bulk, finishing/inspection, and shipping. Where timelines usually slip isn’t the sewing. It’s the interpretation between steps. The Real Tradeoff: Unit Cost vs Coordination Cost Brands that choose overseas clothing production often do so for specialization, material ecosystems, and scalability. For micro-studios, the hidden price is coordination. It shows up as slower feedback loops across time zones, more room for assumptions, and higher impact from late changes that ripple across materials, approvals, and scheduling. This doesn’t make overseas the wrong move. It simply means that teams with a better experience tend to reduce ambiguity early and keep decisions easy to reference later. Choosing Where to Produce Without Getting Lost in “Top Countries” Lists Overseas clothing production content, like “best countries for clothing manufacturing,” can be useful for general awareness. However, boutique brands typically require a more practical filter. What often matters most isn’t whether a country is “top.” It’s whether the factories you can realistically access in that region match your product, your order size, and your release cadence. A Better Shortlisting Lens Location is less of a scorecard and more of a bundle of tradeoffs. Product-category fit tends to matter more than reputation. Some regions have deeper experience in certain categories. If a factory’s strengths don’t match what you’re making, everything gets harder. MOQ reality matters early. If your drops are measured in hundreds rather than tens of thousands, the right region is often the one where you can find factories that take smaller runs seriously. Lead times and shipping lanes shape your calendar. “Good pricing” loses its shine if timelines become unpredictable or freight doesn’t line up with your launch windows. Communication bandwidth is part of the cost. Regions with stronger English support, clearer processes, or more familiarity with Western documentation standards can reduce friction. It’s not a guarantee, but it can improve the baseline. Instead of ‘Top Lists,’ Think in Patterns Here are good starting hypotheses to test against your product, timeline, and factory options. Europe (including Portugal) is often associated with higher quality expectations and smaller-to-mid runs, with pricing that reflects that. Turkey is often discussed as a bridge between speed and capability for certain categories. South Asia can be attractive for certain material ecosystems and pricing, but coordination often matters more. Southeast Asia is frequently chosen for scale and category strengths, with MOQs and lead times that vary widely by factory. China still has deep capacity and specialization in many categories, though some brands weigh trade risk and sourcing strategy more carefully now. For teams shipping multiple drops, nearshore options can also be worth considering as a cadence decision. When rapid sampling cycles matter, being closer can reduce the “two-day delay” effect that comes from time zones and shipping samples back and forth. Finding a Manufacturer That Fits a Micro-Studio Workflow For a boutique brand, the best overseas manufacturer is the one that fits your product and your operating reality. Small teams sometimes think they’re shopping for capacity when they’re really shopping for alignment. A factory can be talented and still be the wrong partner if its workflows don’t match how you work. Where Micro-Studios Typically Find Factories Most teams find manufacturers through referrals, sourcing partners, platforms/directories, trade shows, and industry networks. The channel matters because it changes the signal you get. Referrals often come with context about strengths and limitations. Platforms can surface more options, but usually require sharper filtering and more upfront qualification. What “Fit” Looks Like Beyond Price Fit tends to show up in the details that reduce rework later. Category specialization usually lowers assumptions. Factories that live in your category ask better questions and make fewer “reasonable guesses.” Sampling responsiveness often matters as much as bulk quality. If sampling cycles are slow or revisions are hard to implement, the whole season compresses. Capacity match can be a quiet deal-breaker. If your order size is small relative to a factory’s baseline, you may become low priority even if they accept the work. Process maturity shows up in predictability: how they quote, how they confirm materials, how they handle approvals, and how they track changes. Communication style can make or break the relationship. Factories that flag risks early and ask clarifying questions instead of guessing typically reduce your team’s workload. Red Flags That Often Lead to Delays No single red flag is always fatal, but patterns matter. Delays often start when timelines sound great up front but don’t hold, when answers stay vague about what’s included, or when everything is “no problem” despite missing specs. It can also be telling when a quoting process doesn’t request much detail. If questions aren’t asked early, gaps often get filled later, which is where sampling loops and rework tend to begin. Documentation Clarity Is the Biggest Lever for Reducing Rework If overseas clothing production has a hidden multiplier, it’s interpretation. When you’re not in the same room, the factory has to fill gaps based on experience and habit. It’s what happens when information is almost clear. For boutique brands and micro-studios, clarity matters even more because calendars are tighter. Extra sampling loops don’t just add cost. They compress everything downstream. What Factories Typically Need Factories need enough detail to quote and build without guessing. That usually means clear measurements and size intent, construction expectations (stitching, seam finishes, reinforcements), materials and components (fabric, trims, labels, hardware, thread), artwork placement/files, and packaging/labeling requirements. It doesn’t have to be overwhelming. These are simply the places where misunderstandings tend to live. Why “Almost Clear” Creates Sampling Loops A size chart without tolerance expectations can create a sample that’s “close” but doesn’t feel right. Feedback becomes subjective, and subjective feedback tends to take longer to translate across distance. Construction is similar. “Topstitching” sounds simple until you realize there are choices around width, thread, seam finish underneath, and whether it’s functional or decorative. If those expectations aren’t shared, the factory will choose something reasonable. If it’s not what you intended, you’re back into revisions. A useful way to think about documentation is this: the clearer it is, the less the factory has to interpret. Less interpretation usually means fewer loops. Managing Production Across Time Zones Once you go overseas, time becomes a material. You spend it waiting: for answers, for photos, for revised samples, for confirmation that a change was understood. For micro-studios shipping multiple drops, the goal usually isn’t “perfect speed.” It’s predictable speed. Predictability often improves when decisions are captured cleanly, and there’s a single source of truth. Approvals and Feedback Loops Sampling and approvals are where timelines often stretch. Not because factories are slow, but because questions arrive in bursts: a trim choice needs confirmation, a measurement is unclear, artwork placement needs a quick decision, or a material substitution is proposed. Each question is manageable on its own. The delay comes from how many round trips those questions require across time zones. Many smooth overseas workflows are less about pushing harder and more about reducing ambiguity before sampling starts, then keeping approvals easy to reference once sampling is underway. Version Control A common issue is determining which file is final. Micro-studios often end up with a tech pack that’s been revised multiple times, a spreadsheet with updates, an email thread with key decisions, and a PDF someone exported before the last change. From your side, that can feel manageable because the context is in your head. From the factory’s side, it’s easy to follow the wrong version and still “do exactly what you sent.” This can make overseas clothing production expensive because two truths exist simultaneously. Quality Control When You Don’t Have a Big Team Many boutique brands do quality control informally and often late. However, overseas production raises the stakes because issues can be harder to correct once bulk is underway. That doesn’t mean you need a huge QC operation. It usually means it helps to know where quality tends to drift and where problems are most expensive to discover. Where Quality Typically Slips Quality issues often cluster in a few places. Materials consistency (different fabric lots behaving differently). Measurement tolerances (expectations not aligned). Construction and finishing (details that shape “premium” feel). Labels/packaging (requirements that can block shipping readiness). Common Checkpoints Without the Bureaucracy There are natural moments where quality is easier to assess: aligning expectations before bulk begins, checking output while production is in motion, and confirming finished goods before shipping. Some brands use third-party inspectors at certain stages when the downside of a flawed bulk run would be painful. Others lean on tighter documentation, clearer factory communication, and photo/video verification along the way. A useful question is simply, where would a problem be most expensive to discover? That question often points to the checkpoint that deserves the most attention. Common Pitfalls That Break Timelines Overseas clothing production problems often start small and then stack up. For boutique brands, it’s rarely one dramatic failure. It’s a few manageable issues compounding until the calendar collapses. Misaligned Specs and Versions For example, a factory might be using a tech pack that’s one revision behind, or building to an older measurement note because it was confirmed in an email—but never reflected in the main document. The result can be output that’s faithful to what they received, but misaligned with what your team believes is current. Late Changes and Ripple Effects Late changes are often expensive because they ripple. For instance, fabric substitutions can trigger re-approvals, cost changes, lead time changes, and sometimes fit changes. Artwork changes can affect placement files, labels, and packaging. It all compresses timelines and increases the chance that something gets missed. Factory Fit Mismatch A factory can be excellent and still be the wrong partner if any of the following are true. Your order size is small relative to their baseline. Your category isn’t their core strength. Your cadence requires faster iteration than their workflow supports. Communication bandwidth is limited. In those cases, timelines can break even when quality is fine. Packaging and Labeling Readiness Packaging and labeling can feel secondary during design, but they can later become “stop-the-line” requirements. Hang tags, care labels, fold methods, polybags, carton markings, and barcode expectations can all affect shipping readiness. When these decisions arrive late, they can delay finished goods even if the garments themselves are done. How AI Techpacks Helps Prevent Version Confusion Stress in overseas clothing production usually comes from the information layer around the work. When multiple styles are moving at once, product details often end up scattered across spreadsheets, PDFs, email threads, chat messages, and folders full of exports that look nearly identical. That’s when version confusion starts, and timelines slip. AI Techpacks is designed to reduce that “scattered truth” problem by keeping tech pack specs more centralized and easier to share. It also supports clearer revision visibility (so changes are less likely to get lost between rounds) and helps keep factory communication anchored to the same set of product details. On a small team, that kind of clarity usually saves time in two places: less time spent tracking down the latest details, and less time lost to preventable back-and-forth. AI Teckpacks reduces the unforced production delays caused by scattered information. Overseas Works Best When Clarity Leads Overseas clothing production can be a strong move for boutique brands and micro-studios, especially when you’re aiming for consistent drops and a reliable supply chain. The biggest difference between smooth overseas production and constant firefighting usually isn’t effort. It’s clarity. Distance and time zones don’t create problems on their own. They amplify small gaps in communication and documentation. title: Phunware Announces Appointment of Elliot Han as Chairperson of the Board of Directors
body_text: Phunware Announces Appointment of Elliot Han as Chairperson of the Board of Directors Download as PDF December 02, 2025 8:31am EST Experienced Corporate Finance and Technology/Digital-Asset Leader to Guide Board Strategy and Growth Initiatives AUSTIN, Texas, Dec. 02, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Phunware, Inc. (“Phunware” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: PHUN), the enterprise cloud platform for mobile that provides products, solutions, data, and services for brands to engage, manage and monetize global audiences, today announced that Elliot Han was appointed Chairperson of the Company’s Board of Directors and Chairperson of the Board’s Audit Committee, each effective October 2025. Mr. Han has served as a Class II non-employee Director on the Company's Board since January 2024 and will continue to chair the Board’s Compensation Committee. Since February 2025, Mr. Han has served as Chief Investment Officer of C1 Fund Inc., a NYSE-listed closed-end investment company primarily focused on investments in private digital asset services and technology companies. Since September 2023, he has also served as a Partner at PGP Capital Advisors, a boutique investment and merchant banking firm, focused on the technology and digital asset sectors. Mr. Han is an accomplished investment executive with global experience and deep expertise across technology, finance, digital assets, and the full spectrum of corporate finance, strategy, legal, and operational disciplines. He has held senior leadership roles at several global financial institutions, including Cantor Fitzgerald, the New York Stock Exchange, and Goldman Sachs. He also served on the management team of the Argon Group, a pioneering blockchain technology and advisory company. Earlier in his career, he practiced corporate law at Freshfields Bruckhaus Deringer and began his finance career at Credit Suisse/CSFB. Mr. Han holds a B.A. from Columbia University, a Master's degree from Oxford University, and law and M.A. degrees from Cambridge University. “We are thrilled to have Elliot lead as Chairperson of our Board and Chair of the Audit Committee,” said Jeremy Krol, Interim CEO of Phunware. “Elliot has a wealth of experience in corporate finance, strategy, capital markets, technology and digital assets, and his leadership will continue to be instrumental as we execute on our software business growth strategy, explore and develop opportunities in digital assets, and deliver value to our shareholders.” About Phunware Phunware, Inc. Key metrics available: Performance of all campaigns / automated campaigns / sequences Subscriber growth trends Delivery metrics by email address Performance comparison by time period You can browse the full dashboard and view how metrics change based on your selected date range. 2) Enhanced Sequence Statistics Page The statistics page for individual sequences has been upgraded so that step-by-step metrics (opens, clicks, replies, etc.) are clearer and easier to interpret. Relate Fixed an issue where some email attachments failed to open Fixed errors in 1:1 scheduled email sending Email editor language now follows the browser language Fixed a bug where Documents would open from the middle of the file instead of the first page Spread Improved UI stability for sequences and campaigns Performance optimizations for pages handling large datasets Relate & Spread: Continually Evolving If you encounter any inconvenience or have feature suggestions, feel free to share them anytime. title: Latency Performance Assessment of zerank-2
summary: In this blog, we go over the latency performance of ZeroEntropy's latest reranker model zerank-2.
body_text: TL;DR zerank-2 delivers consistent, low-latency performance under realistic production conditions. In our testing, 97.3% of requests completed under 500ms with zero failures. This document presents our latency measurements and explains how to properly benchmark reranker performance. Why Proper Latency Testing Matters Production RAG pipelines depend on the reranker staying off the user-facing critical path. When evaluating reranker latency, it’s critical that your testing reflects actual production usage patterns. Real user traffic doesn’t arrive at uniform intervals. It comes in bursts and clusters — exactly the dynamic that drives tail latency . Testing with sequential requests or artificial patterns will give you misleading results that don’t predict real-world performance. Our tests use Poisson arrival patterns because they model the random, bursty nature of production traffic. This approach reveals how systems behave under realistic load conditions, including queueing effects, throughput , and concurrent request handling. (NASDAQ: VERU), a late clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing innovative medicines for the treatment of cardiometabolic and inflammatory diseases, today announced multiple presentations at The Society on Sarcopenia, Cachexia, and Wasting Disorders (SCWD) 18th International Conference, and the SCWD’s Regulatory and Clinical Trials Update Regulatory Workshop, both in Rome, Italy. 18 th International Conference of the Society on Sarcopenia, Cachexia, and Wasting Disorders Program Session P: Weight loss drugs and cardiovascular health Presenter: Mitchell Steiner, Veru Inc.’s Chairman, President & CEO Session Date: December 12, 2025 Presentation Number: P3 Presentation Name: The Veru Experience Presentation Time: 4:30 pm – 4:45 pm Central European Time Presentation Location: Hall A, A. Roma Lifestyle Hotel, Rome, Italy Additional information on the meeting can be found on the following website: https://society-scwd.org/annual-conference/ SCWD Regulatory and Clinical Trials Update - Regulatory Workshop Presentation Name: Treatment Approaches to Address Muscle Wasting in the Context of Obesity Therapy & Regulatory Issues Therapeutic approaches to prevent/counteract skeletal muscle loss during incretin therapy – drugs, trial designs, and endpoints. Comments from industry representatives: Lilly approach Veru approach: Mitchell Steiner, Veru Inc.’s Chairman, President & CEO Actimed approach Regeneron approach Academic discussants Regulatory considerations: EMA+FDA representatives General discussion Session Date: December 11, 2025 Session Number: C2 Session Time: 10:15 am - 11:15 am Central European Time Session Location: A.Roma Lifestyle Hotel, Rome, Italy Presentation Name: Possible Endpoints for Regulatory Approval of Treatments Addressing Muscle Wasting in the Context of Obesity Therapy Reviewing possible endpoints Industry viewpoint: Mitchell Steiner, Veru Inc.’s Chairman, President & CEO Regulatory considerations General discussion Session Date: December 11, 2025 Session Number: C3 Session Time: 11:15 am - 11:55 am Central European Time Session Location: A.Roma Lifestyle Hotel, Rome, Italy About Veru Inc. Veru is a late clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing innovative medicines for the treatment of cardiometabolic and inflammatory diseases. The Company’s drug development program includes two late-stage novel small molecules, enobosarm and sabizabulin. Enobosarm, a selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM), is being developed as a next generation drug that makes weight reduction by GLP-1 RA drugs more tissue selective for loss of fat and preservation of lean mass leading to improved body composition and physical function with expected clinically meaningful incremental weight reduction versus GLP-1 RA monotherapy. Sabizabulin, a microtubule disruptor, is being developed for the treatment of inflammation in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Enobosarm Obesity Program - Enobosarm is a next generation drug that makes weight reduction by GLP-1 RA more tissue selective for fat loss – Phase 2b QUALITY clinical study The Phase 2b QUALITY clinical study was a positive multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized, dose-finding clinical trial designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of enobosarm 3mg, enobosarm 6mg, or placebo as a treatment to augment fat loss and to prevent muscle loss in 168 older patients (≥60 years of age) receiving semaglutide (Wegovy®) for weight reduction. After completing the efficacy dose-finding portion of the Phase 2b QUALITY clinical trial ended at 16 weeks, participants continued into a Phase 2b maintenance extension study where all patients discontinued semaglutide treatment, but continued receiving placebo, enobosarm 3mg, or enobosarm 6mg as monotherapy in a double-blind fashion for 12 weeks. The Phase 2b QUALITY and Maintenance Extension clinical trial was a positive study that demonstrated that preserving lean mass and physical function with enobosarm plus semaglutide led to greater fat loss during the 16 week active weight loss period. While weight loss was similar across treatment groups in this short 16 week study, we anticipate that preservation of lean mass and function will lead to increased energy expenditure, and this effect coupled with the direct effects of enobosarm on the additional selective reduction in fat mass will result in incremental weight reduction in a longer clinical study in patients who have obesity. Planned Phase 2b PLATEAU clinical study Veru’s planned Phase 2b PLATEAU clinical study will evaluate the effect of enobosarm 3mg on total body weight, physical function, and safety in approximately 200 patients who have obesity (BMI ≥ 35) and are initiating GLP-1 RA treatment for weight reduction. The primary efficacy endpoint of the study is the percent change from baseline in total body weight at 72 weeks. An interim analysis will be conducted at 36 weeks to assess the percent change from baseline in lean body mass and fat mass, as measured by DEXA scans. The key secondary endpoints are total fat mass, total lean mass, physical function (stair climb test), bone mineral density, and patient reported outcome questionnaires for physical function (SF-36 PF-10, and IWQOL-lite CT physical function). The Phase 2b PLATEAU clinical study is designed to assess the ability of enobosarm treatment to break through the weight loss plateau observed in patients with obesity receiving GLP-1 RA treatment to achieve clinically meaningful incremental weight reduction and preserve muscle mass and physical function by 72 weeks. The clinical study is expected to begin in calendar Q1 2026.
